headlines.article_text: Binance co-founder asks Elon Musk to stop trolling after $6.3 billion hack Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Binance's cofounder Changpeng Zhao urged Elon Musk to stop mocking the exchange after it suffered a $6.3 billion hack. The SpaceX and Tesla CEO posted a series of emojis on X which appeared to poke fun at the attack, which has seen $3 billion in crypto assets frozen so far. In this article SPCX TSLA Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Changpeng Zhao, co-founder of Binance Holdings Ltd., during the Bitcoin Asia conference in Hong Kong, China, on Thursday, Aug. 27, 2026. Chan Long Hei | Bloomberg | Getty Images The cofounder and former CEO of Binance asked Elon Musk not to "troll" the company on Friday and instead "show some support" after the SpaceX CEO appeared to mock the embattled cryptocurrency exchange in a series of social media posts. After learning the world's largest crypto exchange had been hit by a $6.3 billion hack late Thursday, Musk posted several emojis, ranging from laughing to grimacing, on X. In response, Changpeng Zhao reminded the SpaceX and Tesla CEO of Binance's equity stake in Musk's businesses. Binance’s SpaceX stake, which stems from an earlier investment in what was then-Twitter, is worth more than $1 billion, Zhao said. That's a tiny fraction of SpaceX's roughly $2 trillion valuation. "Elon, have a lot of respect for you, but bad time to troll. Please stop," Zhao wrote. "Our SPCX shares (from our $500m investment in your Twitter takeover) are worth more than a billion. Would appreciate if you show a little support. Thanks!" It's not the first time the pair has sparred online. In Nov. 2021, Binance suspended Dogecoin withdrawals because of a wallet glitch, a measure Musk called "shady". In reply, Zhao highlighted a major Tesla recall of almost 12,000 U.S. vehicles due to software glitches and hardware issues. Binance froze all withdrawals and deposits after the hack, which investigators suspect to be the work of North Korean state-sponsored hacking unit TraderTraitor. It has since restored deposits. headlines.article_text: Amazon, Intel shares fall after earnings amid AI spending concerns Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Intel shares fell roughly 29% on Friday and headed for their worst day since 1974. The chipmaker issued weaker-than-expected guidance, citing ongoing softness in the PC market. Amazon also sold off following an earnings miss. In this article AMZN INTC Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan speaks during a keynote presentation at Computex in Taipei on June 2, 2026. Cheng Yu-chen | Afp | Getty Images Intel shares plummeted 29% on Friday and headed for their worst day since 1974 after the chipmaker issued weaker-than-expected guidance due to a plant shutdown in Israel and ongoing softness in the PC market. The stock was on pace for its second-steepest drop on record. It's a major setback for CEO Lip-Bu Tan, who was hired in March 2025, and has since been on a campaign to revive the company after it missed out on the early years of the artificial intelligence boom. Intel's plunge is also a big hit to the Trump administration, which led the U.S. government into taking a 10% stake in the company over a year ago. While it's still a profitable investment, the value of those holdings dropped by about $12 billion on Friday. Nvidia also took a big stake in Intel, and is looking at a $6 billion drop in value. Heading into Thursday's earnings report, Intel shares were up about 150% this year, buoyed by demand for central processors, which are becoming critical to agentic AI workloads. Analysts at D.A. Davidson downgraded the stock to neutral from buy on Friday in a report titled, "Not fixed yet." "We understand the PC market is being impacted at the industry level," the analysts wrote. "However it is hard to justify the current multiple when weakness is so significant." Amazon and Intel stock chart Amazon shares also sold off on Friday, slipping about 1%, after the company reported a third-quarter miss on the top and bottom line while maintaining its capital expenditure forecast for 2026 of $220 billion. Amazon also reported negative free cash flow for the second consecutive quarter, and a big increase from the previous period. The Nasdaq Composite slid more than 2.5%, capping off a week of rough tech earnings. Alphabet on Thursday suffered its worst day on record, plunging more than 12%. The stock fell again on Friday. Other semiconductor names also notched declines. Chip giant Nvidia fell 4%, while Broadcom dropped about 6% and mobile chipmaker Qualcomm tumbled 12%. Not a 'moment of reckoning' Investors are growing nervous about the massive AI spending from the tech giants and whether their investments will pay off. "I don't think this is a moment of reckoning but I think it's a moment where investors should take a long thought about how positioning across the space still remains crowded even though the fundamentals are strong," Matt Orton, chief market strategist at Raymond James, told CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" on Friday. For Intel, the disappointing forecast reflects a PC market that's getting hammered due to soaring costs for memory and other components. Global PC shipments declined 4% in the second quarter from a year earlier, according to Counterpoint Research . Read more CNBC tech news AI build-out hits snag as Google and Microsoft put off raising capex forecasts Trump tech allies swap AI for 'super intelligence' in earnings calls Tech giants need legacy businesses to keep growing as they pour trillions into the AI buildout Nvidia responds to accusations that Jensen Huang was Chinese target Intel said it expects adjusted earnings per share of 25 cents this quarter on revenue between $15 billion and $16 billion. Analysts were expecting revenue of $17.1 billion and EPS of 43 cents, according to LSEG. "We see the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year," Intel finance chief David Zinsner, said in the release. "We will continue making disciplined investments in capacity and working capital to increase supply and support future growth." The guidance also accounts for the effects of an explosion at a fab in Israel that killed two workers and seriously injured a third earlier this month. The incident will cost the company about $600 million in lost revenue over two quarters, Zinsner said. Tan said the explosion, which he called an "unfortunate and tragic accident," caused an "extended shutdown" at the plant, impacting shipments of 10-nanometer chips. Key to Tan's turnaround effort is Intel's foundry business, which has struggled to find its footing. Intel is the only U.S.-based manufacturer of advanced logic chips, and is now in high-volume production of its most advanced 18A chip out of its new fab in Arizona, providing an alternative to Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co . Its next Arizona fab is expected to begin operations by the end of 2028. Intel still has no external customers for its new chips. "We're going to have a couple of customers ready to announce the next two quarters," Tan said on the call, adding that Intel is making "tremendous progress" on its coming 14A chips. headlines.article_text: Stocks making the biggest moves midday: INTC, LITE, SNDK, TWLO, COIN Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Here are some of the companies making headlines in midday trading. Semiconductor stocks — Chipmakers suffered Friday as technology stocks sold off and concern reemerged about the strength of the artificial intelligence trade. The VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) slumped 7%, Astera Labs tumbled 12%, Qualcomm dropped 11% and Nvidia lost 4%. AI infrastructure plays — The iShares A.I. Innovation and Tech Active ETF (BAI) slumped more than 7%, Micron Technology slid more than 5%, Lumentum Holding s by more than 10% and Arista Networks by almost 8%, as stocks tied to the artificial intelligence buildout continued to lose air. CNBC's David Faber also said Friday that the proposed deal for Lumentum by Marvell Technology won't come at a big premium. Regeneron Pharmaceuticals – The biotech company jumped 11%. Third-quarter results beat estimates, with Regeneron earning $20.07, excluding items, on revenue of $5.12 billion. The FactSet consensus sought $16.42 per share and $4.56 billion. For the full-year period, Regeneron is calling for non-GAAP gross margin on net product sales of about 86%, up from its earlier guidance of 84% to 85%. Sandisk — The data storage device manufacturer fell 12% even after reporting an earnings and revenue beat in its fiscal first-quarter financial report. It delivered adjusted earnings of $49.51 per share compared to analysts' estimates for $46.22, per LSEG. Sandisk also announced an eight-for-one forward stock split. Twilio — The consumer engagement platform dropped about 17% after its current quarter guidance reflected slowing organic revenue growth. Twilio sees fourth-quarter revenue in a range of $1.595 billion to $1.605 billion and year-over-year organic revenue growth in a range of 11% to 12%. In the third quarter, however, organic revenue grew 16% year over year. Roblox — Shares of the gaming platform shed 20% after the company gave disappointing guidance for the fourth quarter. Projected bookings for the period range from $1.89 billion to $2.00 billion, while analysts anticipated $2.00 billion. Mondelez International — The company behind Sour Patch Kids and Oreo cookies added more than 3%. Mondelez reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of 78 cents a share, topping the FactSet consensus estimate of 71 cents per share. FedEx Freight — Shares jumped 15% after the freight transportation services business gave strong guidance for the fourth quarter. FedEx Freight expects quarterly revenue between $2.3 billion and $2.37 billion, compared to $2.07 billion a year ago. It anticipates adjusted operating income between $185 million and $205 million, up from $162 million a year prior. Intel — Shares tumbled 29% after the chipmaker issued weaker-than-expected guidance for the fourth quarter . The company sees adjusted earnings per share of 25 cents on revenue ranging between $15 billion and $16 billion. That's below LSEG estimates of 43 cents in earnings per share and revenue of $17.1 billion. Rivian Automotive — The electric vehicle maker jumped over 8% after it reported better-than-expected third-quarter results. Rivian lost an adjusted 48 cents per share on revenue of $2.16 billion. Analysts polled by LSEG expected a loss of 62 cents per share on revenue of $1.99 billion. The company also increased its guidance on deliveries . Amazon — Shares slipped 1% after the e-commerce giant reported third-quarter results that missed analyst expectations. The company also posted negative free cash flow of $42.4 billion for the trailing 12 month period. Reddit — The company announced it will require users to log in to access its social media platform and issued weaker-than-expected revenue guidance for the fourth quarter. Shares tumbled 29%. Crypto-related stocks — Shares of Coinbase and Robinhood shed 12% and 8%, respectively, following one of the largest crypto hacks ever on Thursday when Binance reported an estimated $6.3 billion was affected. The company also estimates roughly $3 billion in cryptocurrency assets were frozen. Chevron — Shares added 1% after Chevron reported its net income surged nearly 200% to $9.9 billion in the third quarter. The company also posted better-than-expected revenue for the period. Exxon Mobil — Shares gained more than 1% after the oil giant's profits doubled to $15.4 billion from $7.5 billion in the year-earlier period. AstraZeneca — Shares of the biopharmaceutical company jumped over 7% following better-than-expected third-quarter earnings. The company reported core earnings of $2.79 per share on revenue of $16.21 billion. Analysts expected a profit of $2.60 per share on revenue of $16.05 billion. — CNBC's Michelle Fox, Scott Schnipper, Nick Wells and Darla Mercado contributed reporting.

headlines.article_text: Oil earnings Chevron (CVX) and Exxon (XOM) Q3 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Profits at the U.S. oil majors' refineries surged as they ramped up production to take advantage of high diesel fuel prices globally. Diesel has surged as Ukraine, Iran and Houthi militants have attacked refineries in Russia and the Middle East. In this article CVX Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 5:14 05:14 ExxonMobil CEO Darren Woods: We are producing record volumes of diesel in North America Squawk Box Chevron and ExxonMobil on Friday reported profits that soared in the third quarter, as their U.S. refineries ramped up production to full capacity to take advantage of high diesel fuel prices. Chevron shares are up nearly 2% while Exxon is more than 1% higher. Both touched all-time highs Friday. The world is facing a fuel crisis as Ukraine, Iran and Houthi militants attack refineries in Russia and the Middle East, reducing global capacity by millions of barrels per day. Importers have increasingly turned to U.S. Gulf Coast refineries for diesel supplies as a consequence. ExxonMobil's profits doubled to $15.4 billion, or $3.72 a share, compared to $7.5 billion, or $1.76 a share, in the same period in 2025. When adjusted for one-time items, it posted earnings of $4.23 a share, soundly beating Wall Street's expectations. "Refining capacity is very tight today," Exxon CEO Darren Woods told CNBC in an interview. "Frankly, diesel is the key crunch point here because it is so critical to economic growth [with] very inelastic demand." U.S. diesel stood at a national average of $6.32 per gallon on Friday, an increase of more than 70% compared to the same period last year, according to AAA. Prices in the U.S. hit a record high in September. Chevron's net income surged nearly 200% to $9.9 billion, or $5.06 a share, compared to $3.5 billion, or $1.82 a share, in the same period last year. When adjusted for one-time items, it reported earnings of $5.28 per share, also beating the Street's expectations of $4.89. "The system is under stress," Chevron CEO Mike Wirth told CNBC in an interview. "We remain in an environment that is fairly fragile." Here's what Chevron and Exxon earned, compared with estimates from analysts polled by LSEG: Chevron earnings per share: $5.28 adjusted, vs. $4.89 expected Chevron revenue: $67.8 billion, vs. $61.6 billion expected Exxon earnings per share: $4.23 adjusted, vs. $4.08 expected Exxon revenue: $113.2 billion, vs. $103.1 billion expected High profits from the largest oil companies at a time of war is politically controversial. President Donald Trump said in August that Chevron and Exxon "were making too much money based on a shortage." The supply disruption began in March after the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran. Profits from Chevron's refining division surged more than 300% to $4.9 billion compared to $1.1 billion in the same period in 2025. Its oil and gas production generated earnings of $5.7 billion, up 70% from $3.3 billion in the year-ago period. watch now VIDEO 3:17 03:17 Chevron CEO Mike Wirth on Venezuela licenses: Output to reach roughly 600k barrels per day by 2031 Squawk on the Street Chevron's U.S. refineries processed record amounts of crude oil at just above 1 million barrels per day, as the facilities ran at 98% capacity. Diesel and jet fuel yields rose more than 10%, Wirth said. Exxon's refining division generated profits of about $7.2 billion in the quarter, outpacing its production business' earnings of about $7.1 billion. Its refining profits have surged nearly 200% to $11.4 billion so far this year compared to $4 billion during the first nine months of 2025. Exxon's Gulf Coast refineries operated at 100% capacity utilization. Those refineries produced "record volumes of diesel" in the quarter, Woods said. Chevron's oil and gas production actually declined slightly to 3.9 million barrels per day compared to about 4 million bpd in the same period last year. The decline was in its international segment due in part to the conflict in the Middle East, while output was largely flat in the U.S. year over year. Exxon has produced about 4.5 million bpd this year, a more than 2% decline from nearly 4.7 million during the first nine months of 2025.
